the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
clock: a device that shows or measures the time
The clock on the wall was running ten minutes fast.
inside: the inner part or area of something
The inside of the cave was cool and damp.
you: used to refer to the person being spoken to
The method also feels worse while you are doing it.
your: belonging to the person being spoken to
Your body keeps time even in a completely dark room.
body: the physical structure of a person or animal
Regular sleep helps the body recover from a long day.
keeps: continues to have, hold, or maintain something (he/she/it)
Regular exercise keeps the body strong and flexible.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
even: used to emphasise something surprising or extreme
Your body keeps track of time even in a dark room.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
dark: having little or no light; deep in colour
The old cellar stayed dark and cool even in midsummer.
room: a space within a building enclosed by walls
She rearranged the furniture to make the room feel larger.
trouble: difficulty, problems, or a source of worry
The trouble starts when its clock and the world's disagree.
starts: The film starts at eight o'clock tonight.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
world: the earth and all its people and things
The trouble starts when the body's clock and the world's clock disagree.
disagree: to have a different opinion from someone else
The two scientists disagree about the cause of the extinction.
put: to move something to a particular position
Please put the books back on the shelf when you finish.
volunteer: a person who does something without being paid or forced
Put a volunteer in a room with no windows and something strange happens.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
windows: openings in a wall for light and air
Put a volunteer in a room with no windows and something strange happens.
schedule: a plan of when tasks or events will happen
The train schedule changes slightly during public holidays.
something: She said something that made everyone in the room laugh.
strange: unusual or surprising; difficult to understand
There was something strange about the silence in the house.
happens: takes place; occurs, third person singular
It happens more often than people realise during exam season.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
still: continuing to be the case; even more so
Despite the rain, the match still went ahead as planned.
go: to move or travel from one place to another
We should go before the traffic gets worse.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
sleep: the natural state of rest with closed eyes and reduced awareness
Most adults need about eight hours of sleep each night.
wake: to stop sleeping, or to cause someone to stop sleeping
They still go to sleep and wake at regular times each day.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
regular: happening often, at even intervals; usual
Regular exercise is one of the best habits for good health.
times: plural of time; particular occasions or periods
This is why recipes that give exact times are unreliable.
rhythm: a regular repeated pattern of movement or sound
The drummer kept a steady rhythm throughout the song.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
quite: to a fairly significant extent; fairly
The soup was quite spicy, but everyone still enjoyed it.
twenty-four: The rhythm is not quite twenty-four hours, but it is remarkably steady.
hours: The meeting lasted several hours longer than expected.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
remarkably: in a way that is unusually striking or impressive
The two brothers look remarkably alike despite the age gap.
steady: not changing, moving or shaking; firm and regular
He kept a steady pace throughout the marathon.
other: different from the one already mentioned; additional
One shoe was blue, and the other was black.
words: It has no words for kitchen tools or playground arguments any more.
runs: uses up completely, or continues operating
The shop often runs out of fresh bread by midday.
own: to possess something, or belonging to oneself
Few families in the village own a car of their own.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
simply: in an easy or straightforward way; just, merely
She simply smiled and walked away without saying a word.
react: to behave in a particular way because of something that happens
Plants react to sunlight by growing towards its source.
daylight: the natural light of the day
The office relies mostly on daylight streaming through the large windows.
predicts: states in advance that something will happen
The app predicts rain within the next hour based on radar data.
temperature: a measure of how hot or cold something is
The nurse checked the patient's temperature before the appointment began.
begins: The film begins with a dramatic scene in the mountains.
rise: to increase, swell, or move upward
Bread dough needs a warm place to rise properly.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
hour: It takes about an hour to drive to the city centre.
or: used to link alternatives or possibilities
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
two: Two things mark it as worth keeping.
before: earlier than a particular time or event
Please arrive at the airport before your flight is due to leave.
normally: in the usual or expected way; under ordinary conditions
He normally leaves for work before seven in the morning.
alertness: the state of being quick to notice and respond
Caffeine gives a short boost in alertness but disrupts later sleep.
climbs: rises or increases in amount or level
Temperature climbs sharply in the hour after sunrise in the desert.
falls: Temperature falls sharply after sunset in the desert.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
because: They cancelled the picnic because it started to rain.
internal: existing or happening inside a person, place, or organisation
The company launched an internal investigation into the missing funds.
cycle: a series of events that repeat regularly in the same order
The water cycle moves moisture between the ocean, sky, and land.
exactly: in a way that is precise or correct in every detail
A fact heard once looks exactly like one that will never be needed.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality
It can be difficult to stay calm during an emergency.
reset: to set something again to its original state
You need to reset the router if the internet stops working.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception
Somebody must repaint the roof every few years.
day: a period of twenty-four hours, or the time when it is light
She spent the whole day preparing for the interview.
light: the natural energy that makes things visible
Soft light filled the room through the open curtains.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
morning: the early part of the day, from sunrise until noon
She likes to go jogging in the cool morning air before work.
particular: specific; distinguished from others of the same kind
This particular recipe calls for a very specific type of flour.
acts: A thick curtain acts as a barrier against the cold draft.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
signal: an event or sound that gives a message or triggers an action
The referee's whistle is the signal for the game to begin.
pulls: uses force to move something towards itself
The magnet pulls the small metal pins across the table.
earlier: before the usual or expected time; at a previous point
We left earlier than planned to avoid the traffic.
late: near the end of a period of time, or after the expected time
They arrived late because of heavy traffic downtown.
night: the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise
The city looked completely different lit up at night.
pushes: presses against something to move it away
Cold weather usually pushes energy prices higher across the country.
later: at a time after the one mentioned
They met again later that year at a conference.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
why: Why does the air above a city stay warm long after sunset?
crossing: the act of going from one side to the other, or a place for doing so
The border crossing was closed for repairs over the weekend.
several: more than two but not very many
Several guests arrived late because of the traffic.
zones: areas with particular features or a specific purpose
Crossing several time zones is uncomfortable for the body's internal clock.
uncomfortable: causing or feeling physical or mental unease
It changes where the effort goes, towards the uncomfortable minutes spent trying to remember.
cannot: used to say that something is not possible or not allowed
Visitors cannot enter the site without prior written permission.
jump: to move suddenly upward or change suddenly
nhảy vọt, thay đổi đột ngột
Prices tend to jump sharply whenever supply falls short.
shifts: moves or changes from one state to another
A cold snap shifts the balance towards heavier clothing sales.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
roughly: The trip takes roughly three hours by car.
fly: to travel through the air, especially using wings or an aircraft
Many birds fly south before the cold weather arrives.
east: the direction from which the sun rises
The hotel windows face east, so the sunrise wakes us early.
across: from one side of something to the other
A narrow bridge stretches across the river near the old mill.
six: She woke up at six every morning to go for a run.
needs: The garden needs watering twice a week during summer.
best: of the highest quality or most excellent
This bakery makes the best bread in the whole neighbourhood.
part: a piece or portion of a whole
Only a small part of the report dealt with financial risks.
week: The loss is fastest at the start, then slows over the following week.
agree: to have the same opinion, or to consent to something
Both sides finally agreed on a fair price for the land.
local: relating to a particular, nearby area
The local council approved plans for a new park.
workers: people who do a job, especially manual or paid work
Night workers face a harder version of the same problem.
face: to be forced to deal with a difficult situation
Small businesses face rising costs again this year.
harder: more difficult or more solid; comparative of hard
The second exam was noticeably harder than the first.
version: a particular form of something that differs from others
The company released a new version of its app last week.
same: They wore the same colour shirts to the reunion.
problem: a matter that is difficult to deal with or solve
The main problem with the plan was its enormous cost.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
asked: put a question to someone or requested something
He asked the librarian where he could find books on astronomy.
alert: quick to notice and respond; watchful
The night guard stayed alert throughout his long shift.
their: belonging to or associated with the people or things just mentioned
The students left their bags in the classroom overnight.
expects: The body is asked to be alert when its clock expects sleep.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
resetting: setting something again to its original state
Resetting the device usually fixes minor software problems.
wrong: not correct or true; not what is required
The popular explanation is wrong, and the real one is stranger.
direction: the way something moves, faces, or is developing
The compass showed we were heading in the wrong direction.
many: Many residents still remember the flood of that year.
never: at no time; not on any occasion
She had never travelled outside her home country before that trip.
fully: The patient has fully recovered from the surgery.
adjust: to change something slightly to make it more suitable
It took her a few weeks to adjust to the new time zone.
after: following in time or place; later than
The shop stays open late after the holiday season begins.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
travel: to go from one place to another, especially over a distance
makes: A short walk after dinner makes falling asleep much easier.
mismatch: a lack of agreement or correspondence between two things
There was a clear mismatch between what was promised and what was delivered.
obvious: easy to see or understand; clear
It was obvious from her face that something was wrong.
wall: an upright structure that encloses or divides a space
Tall buildings bounce heat from wall to wall instead of letting it escape.
says: The report says the population has grown by ten percent.
one: Only one seat was left when we arrived at the theatre.
thing: an object, idea, or matter not named specifically
There's one thing I still don't understand about the plan.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
another: one more, or a different one, of the same kind
Could I have another cup of coffee, please?
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
days: It took several days for the flood water to fully recede.
shift: to move or change gradually from one state to another
Public opinion began to shift after the documentary aired.
slowly: at a slow speed; not quickly
The old man walked slowly along the quiet street.
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
easily: without difficulty; in an easy manner
The instructions were clear, so we assembled the shelf easily.
lengthened: The school day was lengthened by thirty minutes this year.
than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
shortened: made shorter in length or time
Her speech was shortened to fit within the ten-minute limit.
flying: the action of travelling through the air
Flying across several time zones can leave travellers exhausted.
west: the direction where the sun sets
Flying west is usually easier because the body's clock adjusts more easily that way.
usually: A machine that appears to be held up by one principle is usually held up by several.
easier: The new software makes editing photos much easier.
practical: concerned with actual application rather than theory
She gave us some practical tips for managing our time better.
advice: guidance or recommendations offered about future action
Her grandmother's advice on saving money still guides her today.
follows: comes after something in time or order
A short quiz follows each chapter of the textbook.
dull: The old paint on the fence had turned a dull grey.
reliable: able to be trusted to do what is expected
She has always been a reliable and hardworking colleague.
get: to obtain, receive, or come to have something
He hopes to get a promotion later this year.
bright: giving out or filled with a lot of light
The bright morning sun woke her up earlier than usual.
early: before the usual or expected time
She always arrives early for important meetings.
avoid: to stay away from or prevent something happening
Try to avoid busy roads during rush hour if you can.
keep: to continue having or doing something; to maintain
Please keep this document safe until the meeting next week.
weekends: the periods of Saturday and Sunday
Get bright light early, avoid it late, and keep the same hours at weekends.
none: not any of a group of people or things
None of the students had heard of the composer before.
exciting: causing strong feelings of enthusiasm or eagerness
None of the routine daily tasks is particularly exciting.
works: This explains why rereading notes feels productive and works so poorly.
speaks: says words aloud; uses a particular language, or communicates something
This painting speaks to the artist's deep love of nature.
only: and no one or nothing more besides; just
Only a handful of tickets remained by the time we arrived.
language: a system of words used by a community to communicate
Learning a new language takes years of steady practice.
understands: present tense of understand, used with he/she/it
It works because it speaks to the clock in the only language the clock understands.
